diagram_math_checks.result: x is in B_n, p(x) is an arbitrary integer, A_0=A(x) is positive, and x=Delta^{p(x)}A_0. The underbrace identifies A_0 with a_1...a_r in the displayed order. Statement (a),(b) and steps 2.1,4.1 justify these labels; no nonnegative-exponent restriction is introduced.

A_0 notin Delta B_n^+ is exactly Delta not-left-dividing A_0, by def-left-and-right-divisibility-for-positive-braids and F1/F5. Delta is the half twist of def-garside-half-twist-and-simple-positive-braid, not its square. Step 2.1 supplies the condition.

For 1<=i<=r with A_(i-1) != 1, a_i=Delta wedge_L A_(i-1), and 1 prec_L a_i prec_L Delta, as Statement (b) and step 1.2 establish using the positive left-gcd supplier. The figure uses the left meet and makes no right-gcd assertion.

The only arrow runs from the residual A_(i-1)=a_i A_i to its next positive residual A_i, removing its left factor. The prose defines its output as a_i^{-1}A_(i-1). The positive-domain recursion is restricted to the indicated nonempty tails, not a map defined on arbitrary braids. Positivity is step 1.2; uniqueness is left cancellation (F3 and the local cancellation supplier).

Step 1.2 gives strict decrease of the nonnegative integer length at every nonterminal recursion step; step 4.1 then yields A_r=1. The implication in the figure summarizes this repeated-step argument, as the caption states. For r=0 the caption fixes A_0=1 and x=Delta^{p(x)} as in (d)(i); the schematic step is not applied in this case.

The figure asserts no crossing, permutation, global divisibility lattice, or new uniqueness criterion. The original rigorous proof, especially step 5.1, remains unchanged and independent of this schematic.
